title: Five questions to ask before you hire an architect
excerpt: Hiring an architect is one of the most consequential decisions in any build. These five questions will help you find the right one — and avoid the wrong one.
author: Blue Door Architects
body:
Most people hire an architect the same way they hire a contractor — by asking for a quote. That is the wrong starting point.

An architect is not a service provider. They are a thinking partner for one of the largest investments of your life. The right question is not how much, but how do you work.

Here are five questions worth asking before you sign anything.

## 1. Who will actually design my project?

Many firms sell you on the principal and then hand you to a junior. Ask directly: will the partner who meets me be the same person drawing my plans and visiting the site? At Blue Door, the answer is always yes. We are a selective studio for exactly this reason.

## 2. How do you handle changes during construction?

Every build has surprises. What separates a good firm from a bad one is how they respond when reality diverges from the drawing. Ask for an example of a project where something went wrong and how they resolved it.

## 3. Can you show me a project similar to mine?

Portfolios are curated. Ask to see a project of similar scale, budget, and typology — and if possible, ask to visit it or speak to that client.

## 4. What is included in your fee?

Architectural fees vary enormously in what they cover. Clarify: does the fee include interior design, site supervision, contractor coordination, furniture sourcing? Or is it drawings only?

## 5. What does the timeline look like, realistically?

Ask for a phase-by-phase timeline and ask what typically causes delays. An honest architect will tell you. An overconfident one will not.

The right architect will welcome these questions. If they seem impatient or vague, that tells you something important.
